name: Dimapur
description: Largest city and commercial hub of Nagaland, serving as the primary gateway with the state's only airport and major railway station. Located on the Dhansiri River plains near the Assam border; base for exploring Kachari heritage and nearby nature sites.
facts: Only airport and major railhead in Nagaland
Ancient capital of the Dimasa Kachari kingdom
Requires Inner Line Permit for visitors from outside Nagaland
Elevation about 145 m on Dhansiri River plains

name: Kachari Ruins (Dimasa Kachari Monoliths)
description: Medieval archaeological site featuring mushroom-domed sandstone pillars and brick ruins from the 10th–13th century Dimasa Kachari kingdom capital. Located in the heart of Dimapur near the railway station; protected by ASI.
facts: Remnants of Dimasa Kachari capital before Ahom conquest
Unique mushroom-shaped pillars with carvings
Best visited October–March
Near Dimapur Railway Station

name: Nagaland Science Centre
description: Interactive science museum and planetarium promoting scientific awareness with galleries on senses, fun science, and children's exhibits. Located behind Naga Arcade in Half Nagarjan, Dimapur.
facts: Established 2004 under Department of Science & Technology
Includes Taramandal planetarium
Open 10 AM–4 PM, closed Mondays
Entry fee nominal; ideal for families

name: Hong Kong Market
description: Bustling flea market in central Dimapur known for affordable imported clothing, footwear, electronics, and goods from Myanmar, Thailand, and China. Popular shopping destination for locals and visitors.
facts: Grew from Tibetan trader stalls in the 1980s
Bargaining common; wide range of winter garments
Central location near major roads
Open roughly 10 AM–7 PM

name: Dimapur Jain Temple
description: Digambar Jain temple dedicated to Lord Mahavira, established in 1947 by migrant Jain families from Kohima. Features intricate glasswork and multiple tirthankara statues; located on Jain Temple Road.
facts: Built in 1947 after families relocated from Kohima during WWII
Moolnayak is Lord Mahavira
Managed by SD Jain Samaj Dimapur
Open daily

name: Dimapur Ao Baptist Church
description: Prominent Baptist church serving the Ao Naga community in Dimapur, reflecting the strong Christian tradition among Naga tribes. One of the larger churches in the city with community activities.
facts: Founded around 1958 with small congregation, now thousands of families
Key spiritual landmark in multi-tribal Dimapur
Active in community and mission work
Located in River Belt / Duncan Basti area

name: Dhansiri River (Dimapur section)
description: Major river flowing through the plains of Dimapur, offering riverside walks, birdwatching on sandbars, and scenic views near the Assam border. Important for local ecology and recreation.
facts: Key waterway of the Dimapur plains
Popular for winter birdwatching and evening walks
Near the commercial hub and railway line
Best in cooler months

name: Kohima
description: Capital of Nagaland and primary hill-station base for exploring Angami Naga culture, WWII history, and nearby trekking valleys. Perched at about 1,444 m elevation with panoramic views of surrounding ridges.
facts: State capital and largest hill town in Nagaland
Elevation approximately 1,444 metres
Requires Inner Line Permit for non-residents
Base for Hornbill Festival and Dzukou Valley treks

name: Kohima War Cemetery
description: Commonwealth War Graves Commission cemetery on the site of the 1944 Battle of Kohima, commemorating Allied soldiers who halted the Japanese advance. Features terraced graves and the famous tennis-court lines marking the intense fighting.
facts: Site of decisive 1944 Battle of Kohima
1,420 Commonwealth burials plus cremation memorial
Maintained by Commonwealth War Graves Commission
Famous epitaph: When you go home tell them of us and say for your tomorrow we gave our today

name: Kisama Heritage Village
description: Open-air Naga Heritage Village designed as traditional morungs of all major tribes, serving as the primary venue for the annual Hornbill Festival. Located 12 km south of Kohima on the highway toward Imphal.
facts: Main venue for Hornbill Festival (December 1–10)
Replica of traditional Naga village with tribal morungs
Approximately 12 km south of Kohima
Showcases crafts, dances and living Naga culture

name: Khonoma Green Village
description: Western Angami Naga village known as India's first Green Village for community conservation, ban on hunting, and protection of Blyth's Tragopan. Features terraced rice fields, stone fortresses and traditional architecture about 20 km west of Kohima.
facts: India's first officially recognised Green Village
Community ban on hunting protects state bird Blyth's Tragopan
Historic resistance against British colonial forces
Elevation about 1,621 m with terraced fields

name: Dzukou Valley
description: High-altitude valley of rolling dwarf-bamboo meadows and seasonal wildflowers at about 2,438–2,452 m, straddling the Nagaland–Manipur border. Popular multi-day trek destination known for the rare Dzukou lily.
facts: Elevation around 2,438–2,452 metres
Straddles Kohima district (Nagaland) and Senapati (Manipur)
Famous for seasonal Dzukou lily blooms
Best approached from Viswema or Jakhama trailheads

name: Japfu Peak
description: Second-highest peak in Nagaland at 3,048 m in the Barail Range, offering panoramic views including toward Dzukou Valley. Holds the Guinness record for the tallest rhododendron tree and supports rare flora and fauna.
facts: Elevation 3,048 metres; second-highest in Nagaland
Guinness record for tallest rhododendron tree
Approximately 15 km south of Kohima
Trek usually starts from Kigwema village

name: Nagaland State Museum
description: State ethnographic museum on Bayavü Hill displaying artefacts, textiles, weapons, jewellery and traditional objects representing all major Naga tribes. Established in 1970 by the Department of Art and Culture.
facts: Opened to public on 25 November 1970
Comprehensive collection of Naga tribal artefacts
Located on Upper Bayavü Hill in Kohima
Managed by Directorate of Art and Culture

name: Mary Help of Christians Cathedral
description: Roman Catholic cathedral of the Diocese of Kohima, noted for architecture blending traditional Naga house elements and a large carved wooden crucifix. Consecrated in 1991; partly funded as a memorial related to the Battle of Kohima.
facts: Consecrated January 1991
Features one of Asia's largest carved wooden crucifixes
Architecture incorporates traditional Naga house motifs
Seat of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Kohima

name: Dzüleke Village
description: Small Angami eco-tourism village in western Kohima district at about 2,130 m, known for community conservation, ban on hunting, homestays and forested surroundings. Name refers to underground water sources.
facts: Population around 156 (2011 Census)
Community ban on hunting since 1999
Elevation approximately 2,130 metres
About 40 km west of Kohima via Khonoma

name: Touphema Tourist Village
description: Community-run heritage village recreating traditional Angami Naga settlement with thatched huts, local cuisine and cultural performances. Located about 36–41 km from Kohima, offering immersive rural tourism experiences.
facts: Model of community-based tourism
Approximately 36–41 km from Kohima
Traditional huts and ethnographic museum on site
Popular for cultural evenings and local Naga food
